scope: v13 and v14 of the Quran-commentary workflow. Repo root R = /Volumes/OZTURK/_projects/prose_generation; all paths below are relative to R unless absolute. v13 = _commentary/v13: DESIGN.md, HANDOFF.md, EVAL_ANCHORS.md, prompts/{act,net,qeq,write}.md, packet.py, run.py, work/ (S1 window plus 1:1-1:7, and the 18:76-105 window plus 18:96), and the arms out, out-max, out-v2, out-xhigh, out-mixed, out-v3, out-v4 with their *.status.json, *.run.log and check files. v14 = _commentary/v14: DESIGN, HANDOFF, COMPARISON, INPUT_AUDIT, STABILIZATION, STABILIZATION_COMPARISON, REVIEW_RESPONSE, ARGUMENT_TRIAL/COMPARISON, BLIND_29_38(+_RESULT), COMPOSITION_TRIAL/RESULT, the scripts (run, synthesis, sources, experiment, review, input_audit, composition), baseline.manifest.json, eval/regressions*.json and the new arms out-sol-max, out-sol-stable, out-sol-argument, out-astra-argument, out-blind-29-38-upstream, out-astra-blind-29-38 and out-sol-astra-composition-29-38. v14/out, out-max, out-v2, out-xhigh and out-mixed are byte copies of v13 taken at commit 522a4321d (v14/baseline.manifest.json: source ../v13, 308 files). They were not re-analysed. I read all design, handoff and result documents and every prompt, and skimmed the scripts. I computed costs and tokens from every *.status.json with my own script (scratchpad phase1/v13-v14/costs.py), and counted records, memory flags, network images and prose words myself. v13 (Claude/Opus lane) and v14 (a separate "primary agent" lane that ran Sol/Astra agents through a "collaboration facility") ran concurrently on 2026-09-27; which model ran the v14 primary agent is unknown. Luna was not used in either version.

models_and_cost:

- v13: Opus 5.5 (claude-opus-5-5, Claude Code 2.1.283, init record in *.log.jsonl) via `claude -p`, no tools. Effort high by default, with xhigh and max arms. Caveat: the xhigh/mixed statuses were recomputed at 15:05 and say "high"; the arm tags and run logs are the evidence for xhigh.

north_star_scorecard.evidence: v13/HANDOFF.md 'Where we are': 'Ground (plain sense, not disorienting) | good (all arms)'. v14/COMPARISON.md: 'Plain sense and neighbours | Preserved'. v14/ARGUMENT_COMPARISON.md: preserved in both Sol and Astra. v14/BLIND_29_38_RESULT.md: 'Plain reading and local context | Strong'. v14/COMPOSITION_RESULT.md: orientation improved. Caveat: v13/EVAL_ANCHORS.md finds v2's 600-900-word paragraphs disorient 'by shape'.

v13/HANDOFF.md: 'What Turkish loses ... good, better than v12'; first-run 1:6 has 'the best Turkish-loss layer (sırat bridge vs sword, hidayet, doğru/istikamet, the two articles)'. v13/out/s018/18_96/18_96.reading.tr.md ¶41: 'Türkçe meal "Körükleyin" der ve Arapçanın adını anmadığı bir alet ekler'. v14 regressions criterion s001_006_turkish_loss is preserved in every Sol/Astra arm (COMPARISON.md, ARGUMENT_COMPARISON.md). Exception: composition dropped 'Ziynet's named Turkish comparison, sebil's fountain sense and the mesken/miskin relation' (COMPOSITION_RESULT.md).

v13/HANDOFF.md: 'Local resonance ... good (step 1 + prose)'. Step 1 yields 31-66 records per ayah, including local, window and scene kinds (v13/out/test1.run.log). Astra blind 29:38 develops house/seam/eye-film and road/water within the 29:37-41 window (BLIND_29_38_RESULT.md).

The chains are found and planned; the landing is where it fails.
- Channel review is pushed as 'strong input: articulate, extend and connect it; do not audit it' (prompts/act.md). The network assembles 'the images v12 lost (road, herd, water, womb, benefaction circuit, swallowing passage)' (HANDOFF.md).
- First-run prose 'lost what the funnel had found': plans skipped member ayat and assemblies did not assemble.
- v2 forced landing into a catalogue; v2's 1:4 water assembly was a 'roll-call that names later ayat's members' (DESIGN §12). v4's cap pushed 17 develops into 1:6 (EVAL_ANCHORS v4).
- 'The water system still does not land as a system' in any arm (HANDOFF.md; STABILIZATION_COMPARISON.md: 'The full rain–well–beam–watering system is not explained').
- True progressive disclosure became possible only with the v3 sequential writes (EVAL_ANCHORS v3: '1:6 refers back to 1:5's trodden road ... in clauses').

Strong where it was tested. 18:96 nafakha was found from the concordance: F4 'Of 20 uses ... 12 are the horn blast, 5 are breath/spirit blown into a formed body ... 1 is here' (v13/out/s018/18_96/act.md), and it landed in the prose (¶41, ¶49). HANDOFF.md: 'No earlier version had this'. More loaded patterns in the same file: zubar, ṣadaf, ḥadīd, afrigh, qiṭr. 18:86 ḥamaʾ was never tested ('not yet tested', HANDOFF.md). The rare-lemma concordance gap is open (INPUT_AUDIT.md).

The rule is in every writer brief ('never "not X but Y"', v13/prompts/write.md; v14/prompts/write.md). A recorded violation in v13 v3 1:6: 'a "not X but Y" against an attested branch ("itmek ya da sürmek değildir" vs the driven hady)' (DESIGN §12; v3 1:6 reading ¶11). v14 criterion s001_006_coexistence was preserved in all Sol/Astra 1:6 arms (COMPARISON.md, ARGUMENT_COMPARISON.md).

Step S was never built. v13/HANDOFF.md: 'Surah commentary ... **not built** (step S)'. v14/DESIGN.md: 'Surah writing ... remain outstanding'. Only English S1 network records exist, with a purpose per image, e.g. 'This is the surah's single petition. Everything before it ... supplies a road part' (v13/out-v4/s001/network.md). Handforward and deferred material has no consumer.

Measured $3.7-5.8 per ayah (first run) and $4.6-6.8 (v2) via claude -p (my sums from the status files), against the ~$1 aim. HANDOFF.md: 'Economics ... not met (≈ $4.5–7 via claude -p; ≈ half via batch)'.
- xhigh roughly doubles or triples the cost; max failed at $10.28.
- Batch/cache_control was never built, and claude -p gave 0 prefix hits (DESIGN §9).
- Writer inputs grew instead of funnelling: 149 → 235 KB in v13, 201-207 KB in v14.
- v14 Sol/Astra costs are unknown; the 29:38 Opus upstream alone was $4.41 before any writer.
- The funnel principle holds only upstream: compact English records of 17-42 KB per ayah.

recorded_verdicts.verdict: The funnel's split is right: generative discovery (step 1) and the network are strong and recover what v11/v12 audited away ... The weak joint is the handover from records to prose. The first run under-delivered (things found, then dropped); the v2 fix over-delivered (everything forced in, catalogue-sized).

Recommendation: high for the per-ayah steps; test xhigh for the network alone (one call per surah); fix the must-land list first. The length of the three new versions is the must-land overshoot, not effort.

v2 has no content regression against the first run ... The 'first-run 1:6 is the richest' judgment is about form, not content ... 'regression' in this project has two axes that must be scored separately: anchors (recall) and form ... Effort above high buys little on anchors.
the ranked budget bought form at the price of recall: −3 to −4 anchors on 1:5, −8 on 1:6. The trade is not acceptable as it stands for 1:6 (below the first run).
Against the first run v4 is one anchor short and 1,700 words longer; against Sol it is one anchor short with 3.6× the checkable tags and headings.

v3 did not remove the catalogue, it re-shaped it: root/branch mentions per 1,000 words are 10.2 (first run), 13.6 (v2), 17.5 (v3), 7.6 (Sol) ... For the reader the first run's 1:6 is still the best of the three ... v14's JSON account is the accounting trap (51% of Sol's output bytes; 180 of 192 items claimed 'connected').

The eight predeclared preservation criteria survive; the two improvement criteria show progress. The candidate remains unaccepted: four Arabic quotations differ from the verifier's spelling conventions.

The same Sol max model can produce exact tagged sources and substantially smaller accounting ... It still omits an earlier explanatory connection while claiming the larger source record is connected ... not evidence that the remaining synthesis problem is solved or that a model ceiling has been identified.

The project's NORTH_STAR.md does state an Opus-high production preference based on older runs. That is a prior project decision, not a fresh controlled finding that this Sol writer cannot transfer ... A model limitation remains possible; this comparison has not established it.

Astra is the stronger candidate in this matched run ... Neither candidate is accepted: both lose the explicit connection between the trodden road surface, the signs and the centre line ... The prompt and the writer both matter.

Astra produced a substantial, well-grounded reading from the unchanged v14 single-ayah path ... It remains experimental: two invalid trace anchors fail the structural check, and the reading still contains serial excursions and unresolved deferrals. This result does not establish reliable blind generation for arbitrary ayat.

The old design encouraged exhaustive representation and produced a catalogue. This design successfully removes that pressure, but does not reliably distinguish an expendable association from a consequential supported surprise ... We shifted from excessive inclusion to consequential exclusion.
Failed treatment: substantially clearer and shorter, but loses the predeclared supported lexical contribution. Stop this variant under the agreed rule.
the funnel does not need a broad rewrite for this trial. The writer handover needed an outcome-based revision. The inherited upstream has specific gaps to fix and test separately before production.

Under the agreed stopping rule, stop this treatment: no prompt tuning, target-specific restoration or new call starts automatically ... Production requirement clarified by the user: this pipeline must run blind for any supplied ayah.

failure_modes: Handover loss (records → prose): items found upstream are dropped, turned into caveats or reversed, and assemblies are not assembled (v13/HANDOFF.md).
Obligation-list catalogue: 'every item lands' produced 49-144 items and 5-8K words with 900-word paragraphs (v13/HANDOFF.md; EVAL_ANCHORS.md).
Budget-driven recall loss: the ranked budget demoted the images that carried the anchors (EVAL_ANCHORS.md v3).
Script-proxy bugs silently deciding content: mustland counted entries instead of distinct words, the staging regex missed double tags, and demotions were unrecorded (v13/DESIGN.md §12).
Role caps displacing work: an assembly cap produced 17 develops at 1:6 and a serial tour (EVAL_ANCHORS.md v4).
Roll-call assemblies that name later ayat's members (v2's 1:4 water; DESIGN §12).
An image never assembled as one scene across any arm (the water system: rain, gathered water, well, beam), plus misuse of a member (B012 as a sword hilt in v2 1:6) (EVAL_ANCHORS.md G023).
CLI 64K-per-response cap: max effort was all thinking and failed; QeQ was capped 4 times, forcing a QeQ trim (DESIGN §10; HANDOFF.md).
429 session limits refused 5 calls at $0 (out-v2.run.log; out-mixed.run.log).
Estimator blind to output growth: xhigh write $5.90 against an estimate of $2.39; mixed QeQ $4.87 against $1.42 (status files).
Cost double-counting over resumed parts, fixed later (HANDOFF.md traps).
No prefix caching via claude -p (DESIGN §9).
Writer self-accounting bloat and overclaiming: 51.4% of output, 180/192 'connected' (v14/COMPARISON.md).
Source-convention mismatch: concordance spelling differed from the verifier's (4 failures) (v14/COMPARISON.md).
Multi-part records hide omitted components: a 'linked' record does not mean it was explained (v14/ARGUMENT_COMPARISON.md).
Writer compression drops explanations even after retrieving the source (Sol: 18:1-2, 20:10, 17:97) (ARGUMENT_COMPARISON.md).
Word mislocation: Sol placed 'âlemler' and 'sahip' in 1:5 (ARGUMENT_COMPARISON.md).
Early selection pruning a supported surprise with no discoverable cue downstream (composition) (COMPOSITION_RESULT.md).
Trace anchor punctuation mismatch leaves 4 IDs unreported (Astra blind) (BLIND_29_38_RESULT.md).
Broken Turkish transliteration that the verifier cannot see ('sebbel tü', 'müm teli'') (BLIND_29_38_RESULT.md).
Persistent serial touring and excursions in both Sol and Astra (ARGUMENT_COMPARISON.md; BLIND_29_38_RESULT.md).
Containment violations, unsupported bridges, first-person hedges and workflow words in the prose (v13/DESIGN.md §12).

Missing evidence lines: branches embedded in finding text but absent from branches.md; variant evidence absent; rare lemmas hidden by the concordance threshold (v14/ARGUMENT_COMPARISON.md; INPUT_AUDIT.md).
The concordance was specified in the v13 brief but never supplied to the v13 writer until v3 (v14/INPUT_AUDIT.md: 'Writer never received it in v13 despite being told to use it').
Narrow acceptance gates: the ten-case gate returns 'eligible: true' while real losses exist (STABILIZATION_COMPARISON.md).
One-sample decisions: 'two replicates per decisive comparison' was listed as not done (v13/DESIGN.md §12); run-to-run variance of the network (15/25/23/28 images) was never measured.
dilution_evidence: More obligations raised recall and destroyed form. v2's must-land list (1:6: 119 items) lifted 1:6 anchors from 23 to 27 but produced 7,451 words with a longest paragraph of 897 (v13/EVAL_ANCHORS.md). The 'richest' first run (149 KB input, no mustland) had the best form.
Fewer obligations restored form and lost recall: v3 went from 27 to 19 anchors on 1:6 (EVAL_ANCHORS.md). No v13 contract got both.

More instructions and inputs to the writer did not buy anchors. v4 input was 235 KB (network.view 60 KB plus previous 38 KB plus mustland) against 149 KB in the first run, yet 1:6 scored 22/7/1 against the first run's 23/4/3 (out-v4/s001/1_6/write.status.json; EVAL_ANCHORS.md).
More thinking did not buy anchors. xhigh and mixed 1:5 scored 18 and 20 against v2's 19 at 3.4x and 2x cost; max failed outright (EVAL_ANCHORS.md; DESIGN §10).

Step 1 with a large packet (60-161K tokens including 25-62 KB of HFT and a 63-156 KB window scan) still found 'nearly every gold and anchor item' (HANDOFF.md). Bulk input did not visibly hurt discovery; the harm appears at synthesis. Inference: dilution is a synthesis-stage problem.
Full previous prose (49 KB) was supplied for continuity; 'It sometimes retells material too' and 'no ablation establishes that the entire preceding essay was necessary' (v14/COMPARISON.md).

Retrieved or available input does not mean it was used. Sol retrieved 18:1-2 and 20:10 and still omitted them (STABILIZATION_COMPARISON.md; ARGUMENT_COMPARISON.md). 'Large research retention is not itself evidence that its distinctive material reaches the reader' (COMPOSITION_RESULT.md).

Output breadth tracked input breadth. Astra with the full 181 KB index plus 94 KB of lookups wrote 6,509 raw words in 60 paragraphs with excursions; with a 66 KB selected packet it wrote 1,374 words in 15 paragraphs and lost the rare-sense surprise (BLIND_29_38_RESULT.md; COMPOSITION_RESULT.md). Inference: neither extreme meets NS7; the missing piece is payoff-aware selection that protects supported surprises.
An extra step can hurt. The added Sol synthesis stage made its omission decisive for the downstream writer (COMPOSITION_RESULT.md).

Compaction without a quality test: the 18:96 step-1 input went from 594 KB to 350 KB by using branch_table instead of section_dictionary and compacting pairs (DESIGN §8). No before/after quality comparison was recorded.
Quoted in v13/DESIGN.md §1 (from w10, outside my scope): '4:34: cold Opus 8 anchors, with the dictionary 5, with the full package 5'.
luna_evidence: Luna: not used in v13 or v14 ('Luna is not used in v13', v13/HANDOFF.md standing rules; 'Dropped: ... Luna as a nominator', v13/DESIGN.md §7). No Luna evidence in this scope.

Sol (gpt-6-sol, max) did well on paragraph discipline (median paragraph 113-164 words, longest 151-280), the lowest catalogue proxy (7.6 per 1,000 words, DESIGN §12), exact sources once the packet and verifier agreed (23/23, then 110 tags), and a clear opening, gift circuit and balance/reckoning (v14/COMPARISON.md, STABILIZATION_COMPARISON.md, ARGUMENT_COMPARISON.md). Its 1:6 anchor score was 23/6/1 on the v13 30-anchor sheet, equal to the Opus first run's 23 integrated and below Opus v2's 27 (EVAL_ANCHORS.md).

Sol did badly at compressing distinct explanations away, including requested and retrieved ones (Book 18:1-2, fire 20:10, face-down 17:97). It deferred the well frame as adding 'no direction'. It mislocated words to the wrong ayah. It overclaimed 'connected' (180/192) (ARGUMENT_COMPARISON.md; COMPARISON.md). As synthesizer in the composition trial it selected 19 of 169 records and dropped the rare-sense tent-seam/eye-film relation, building 'chiefly from Quranic narrative and wording relationships' (COMPOSITION_RESULT.md).

Astra (gpt-6-astra, max) did well: 'stronger retention, source caution and functional development' ('Durmak, burada hareketin koşuludur'). It used 90:10 to keep the direct-object claim from becoming mechanical. It reported source gaps (gh-d-b B004) instead of inventing. In blind 29:38 it carried rare dictionary senses (51 dictionary tags) and kept the upstream corrections (ARGUMENT_COMPARISON.md; BLIND_29_38_RESULT.md). As a prose-only writer after Sol it 'preserves the valuable connections Sol did supply' and 'does not introduce the decisive regression' (COMPOSITION_RESULT.md).

Astra did badly on length (6.4-6.5K raw words), serial excursions, broken transliteration, and a trace anchor punctuation failure. It lost the trodden-surface connection in 1:6 and made no extra lookups when given a selected packet (ARGUMENT_COMPARISON.md; BLIND_29_38_RESULT.md; COMPOSITION_RESULT.md).

No Opus control was ever run on the v14 handover: 'an Opus control would be a separate authorized experiment' (v14/DESIGN.md). So the v14 evidence cannot say whether Astra matches or beats Opus-high on synthesis. This leaves NORTH_STAR's 'Sol and Astra (v5's S1) did not reach it' unretested on matched inputs (REVIEW_RESPONSE.md). Sol and Astra cost per ayah is unknown.
pretraining_vs_data_evidence: Pushed dictionary data made the difference for rare senses. In 29:38, Opus step 1 found F74 'بصيرة is defined as the join between the two panels of a house (tent)' (ب ص ر B006) and F75 'The path-word's eye-disease is defined as a film "like a spider's weaving"' (س ب ل B010), copied from dictionary anchors (v14/out-blind-29-38-upstream/s029/29_38/act.md lines 75-76). This is the NORTH_STAR's own example of a rare sense a model will not recall ('the eye disease in as-sabīl'). It reached the reader only when the writer had the dictionary lines (Astra blind: 51 dictionary tags). It was lost when the selection dropped the branches (composition: 0 dictionary quotations).

Pushed concordance data made the difference for loaded words and counts. 18:96 F4's exact distribution (20 uses: 12 horn, 5 breath, 2 Isa, 1 craft) and further loaded patterns (zubar 10/11 scripture; ṣadaf 4/5 turning away; ḥadīd 14/25 limits) come from concordance.md (v13/out/s018/18_96/act.md). The write brief makes the concordance the only authority for counts (v13/prompts/write.md). The QeQ legacy digest counts conflicted with it (h-d-y 308/316; q-w-m 643/660; v14/INPUT_AUDIT.md).

Pretraining sufficed to locate QeQ passages. The QeQ brief says 'Work from your knowledge of the whole Quran' with references only (v13/prompts/qeq.md). It produced 54-76 annotation lines per ayah, and staging passages like 28:22, 20:10 and 17:97 were found. Exact Arabic still needed a source: every quotation was checked against the canonical text, and Sol's 4 mismatches came from input spelling, not memory (v14/COMPARISON.md). v14 added exact lookup because 'Most QeQ entries give references and English descriptions, not retrieved Arabic' (INPUT_AUDIT.md).

Memory contributes a notable share of discovery (my counts of 'memory: yes' flags): 44 of 408 first-run step-1 records (10.8%) across 1:1-1:7 and 18:96; 11 of 71 (15.5%) in xhigh 1:5; 16 of 86 (18.6%) in 29:38. The flag is used mostly for Quran cross-references recalled from memory (e.g. v13/out/s001/1_3/act.md F11 'people ask one another by God and by the wombs'), not for invented senses. unknown_branches was [] in every act.check.json, so the dictionary guard held.

Model knowledge supplied the loaded-word idea but not its evidence. The brief asks for 'the share (e.g. 11 of 13 uses)' and the model computed it from the pushed clauses (v13/prompts/act.md; act.md F4).

Grammar and Turkish loss came largely from pretraining plus word notes (no grammar DB in the packet). They were rated 'good, better than v12' (v13/HANDOFF.md). Inference: the model's own grammar knowledge suffices for NS2 without pushing the grammar attachment records.

Mechanism and scene knowledge (the well needs its rope and pulley) is pretraining. The designers removed such examples from the briefs as known-answer leaks (v13/DESIGN.md §8), and step 1 still assembled the water system's members, including the well-frame (HANDOFF.md). Inference: the model supplies the mechanism schema; the dictionary supplies the rare members.

key_lessons: Q1: Discovery is not the bottleneck. Opus-high step 1, on a big deterministic packet, found nearly every gold/anchor item for S1, the rare-sense tent seam and eye-film for 29:38, and the loaded word nafakha for 18:96 (v13/HANDOFF.md; v14 29:38 act.md F74/F75). Every loss happened at the records-to-prose handover. The unharvested value is in synthesis selection and in the never-built surah commentary (NS12).

Q1/Q4: Every handover contract tried trades recall against form, with no contract achieving both. Obligation lists gave a catalogue (v2). Budgets and caps lost recall or produced serial tours (v3, v4). A lossless index plus a strong writer gave retention with touring (Astra). Upstream selection gave clarity and lost the surprise (composition). This is iterative contract tuning hitting a wall, as the user suspects. Inference: a qualitatively different selection mechanism is needed, one that ranks by payoff for the primary reading while protecting rare-sense cross-definitions from being cut, and that keeps unselected material visible downstream.

Effort above high is not the lever. xhigh and mixed added scenes, not anchors, at 2-3.4x the cost. Max failed under the CLI's 64K per-response cap (EVAL_ANCHORS.md; DESIGN §10). Thinking is already 62-78% of output at high.

Q2a: Push data where the model cannot recall it: dictionary branches for rare senses (29:38 eye-film/tent seam) and concordance clauses for counts and loaded roles (18:96). Let pretraining supply Quran cross-references (QeQ worked from memory, references only) and mechanism schemas, and verify exact Arabic by lookup afterwards (v14 sources.py). About 11-19% of discovery records lean on memory, flagged (my counts). The dictionary guard held: zero unknown branches.

Q2b: The labelled material in this scope is small and concentrated. About 565 discovery records (branch + trigger + anchor) cover 9 ayat; there are 4 S1 networks, QeQ relation labels for 6 ayat, 52 hand-scored anchors (1:5/1:6), 15 regression criteria (1:6), 5 writer lookup logs and 6 writer traces. That is enough for an eval set for a retriever or distance model, not for training one.

Q3: The composition experiment is the closest analogue to 'a new step on top of existing upstream': a cheaper or different model selects, then a strong writer writes. It failed because the first stage's selection was decisive and invisible downstream (COMPOSITION_RESULT.md). Any step added on top of v5/Luna outputs must hand forward a discoverable index of what it did not select and protect rare-sense findings. Otherwise it reproduces this failure.

Q4: Writer model matters on a fixed packet. Astra retained and developed more than Sol, and Sol compressed away even retrieved explanations (ARGUMENT_COMPARISON.md). No Opus control was run, so the NORTH_STAR claim that only Opus-high synthesizes is untested on the v14 handover. Astra's cost per ayah is unknown.

Q5: The only similarity measure in the path is V9's pairs (reciprocal-rank affinity over a global branch-image network, v9/prepare.py:212-222). It was used as candidate ordering and never ablated or evaluated. The step-1 records (branch pairs that formed images, with the activating word) are a ready test set for any new quran-slm distance: does it rank those partners above the scan's other branches?

Measurement lesson: regression needs at least two axes, anchors (recall) and form (words, paragraph length, catalogue proxy of root/branch mentions per 1,000 words). A narrow predeclared gate or writer self-accounting overstates coverage (EVAL_ANCHORS.md; STABILIZATION_COMPARISON.md). Writer self-accounting also costs 20-51% of output (v14 metrics).

Economics lesson: the funnel compressed upstream records (17-42 KB per ayah) but writer inputs grew (149 → 235 KB), and claude -p gives no caching. Measured $3.7-6.8 per ayah list price. Reaching ~$1-2 requires the Batch plus cache_control path, which was designed but never built (DESIGN §9), and smaller writer inputs.
